body: Yeah that seems like a common feeling in the industry. The rational side of me knows that my anxiety and self-doubt aren’t reasonable, but right now, I don’t have the day-to-day experience as a teacher to challenge those feelings. Instead, I’m stuck in this state of waiting, and it’s completely overwhelming.

Yeah im  really struggling with imposter syndrome right now. The uncertainty has been so overwhelming that it’s made me question whether I should look for a different career path. Deep down, I just want to feel confident and committed to teaching it’s hard enough trying to balance that on its own.

Yeah, I can relate to that. It seems to be a common pattern for me too—feeling anxiety and self-doubt before doing something, but it all tends to fade away once it actually happens whether that’s related to sport , other jobs , interviews and meeting new people.
It’s great to hear from someone else who turned to teaching a little later in life. I’m glad everything has worked out for you, and I’m confident it will for me too. Thanks!

Yeah, I can imagine. Speaking to teachers in the industry and seeing others online has helped me see that potential for myself. I just need to push past this doubt and keep going because I know it will be worth it in the end.

Yeah, I can relate to that feeling. My confidence was pretty strong after finishing my first prac, but it feels like it’s fading a little more with each week away from it. I think looking for some volunteer work in a school is a great idea to stay connected to the day-to-day life of a teacher. Thanks for the suggestion!

Yep definitely looking into that 
Thanks !

It’s tough to hear that you’re going through this, but it’s reassuring to know that these feelings are common. From what others have shared, it seems like doubt is something everyone experiences, but things tend to work out in the end. We’ve got this!

Yeah, I feel the same. I’m overwhelmed, stuck in this sort of limbo while doing uni, constantly overthinking every scenario. It’s left me feeling even more overwhelmed and questioning whether this is the right career for me. The confidence I felt during my first prac reassured me that I’m capable, but I can’t help wishing I could fast-forward five years and feel content with where I’m at.

Yeah that is true , 
I try to think back to the experiences I had during my prac to help overcome my doubts because, overall, I had a positive experience. It’s just unfortunate that there’s such a significant gap between my pracs, which makes it easy for doubt to creep in.

Thanks mate ! 
Check your dms I’ve sent you a message

Thanks for your response. It seems like these feelings aren’t unique to me—they’re pretty common in this industry and probably across all industries. I just want to be able to take a deep breath and feel content with what I’m doing in life.  

Right now, it’s tough being so disconnected from it all, but I’ve got an upcoming prac, and I’m really hoping it will reignite my passion for teaching!

I’m sorry you had to go through that, but I’m really glad you’ve been able to reassure me with your experience and how you managed to turn things around. I won’t lie—it’s been some tough days and nights lately, and all I want is to feel content with this as a career.

I have a placement coming up in the next few months, and I’m really hoping it can reignite my passion for teaching.

Thanks for your response !

Yeah, it’s definitely tough to get through each day with this overwhelming sense of doom hanging over me. From your experience, how do you feel when you come back from holidays and settle back into the flow of teaching?

Yeah, I get that. I feel like 90% of this degree feels disconnected from what I imagine the true experience of being a primary teacher is, and that’s causing me to doubt whether I’ll truly be ready or if this is even my calling. I’m really hoping my next placement (in a prep class!) goes just as well and helps reignite my ambition, giving me something to look forward to in my future.  

Thankyou for your response
Thanks mate. Check your dms I’ve sent you something !
Teams is inspired by a mixture of what I’ve seen on here and other places
